outcome: parental pediatric feeding problems and strategies
cohort: The study included 150 children aged 6-11 years diagnosed with various developmental disabilities (ASD, ADHD, intellectual disability, cerebral palsy, specific language disability, and Down syndrome) from the Child Developmental Center of Safdarjung hospital.
finding: The study found significant associations between behavioral pediatric feeding problems with maternal occupation, child's nutritional status, and child's diagnosis, and between parental pediatric feeding problems and strategies with mode of delivery, child's nutritional status, child's diagnosis, and socioeconomic status.
mod_finding: Mode of delivery (P = 0.016) was found to be statistically significant in its association with parental pediatric feeding problems and strategies among children with developmental disabilities.
cross-section timing: Children aged 6-11 years at the time of data collection
